world.bio: Callum Reyes, 38, jazz guitarist based in Newtown, Sydney. Play in two trios and a quartet, teach twelve students a week, and tour when the band gets booked: Melbourne, Adelaide, a festival in Byron, once a month somewhere. When I'm away the spare room in my rented terrace is on Airbnb, and the hosting income covers a big share of my rent. Recording an album with a trio, due late November.
skills_assets: Jazz guitarist, ten years gigging in Sydney and Melbourne, Berklee online diploma
Plays a 1978 Ibanez semi-hollow and a Gibson ES-175 reissue, both in good order
Teaches guitar to twelve students weekly out of the front room, $60 an hour
Spare room in a Newtown terrace, queen bed, ensuite shared, 4.9-star Airbnb listing with Superhost status
A trio called Monday Ghosts, and a quartet that does weddings for the rent
Tour van-sharing arrangement with the bassist, a 2012 Toyota HiAce

projects.name: Monday Ghosts debut album
projects.text: Recording a debut album with a trio at a studio in Marrickville, ten originals. Tracked six so far. Mixing in October, mastering in November, pressing 300 vinyl via a plant in Melbourne. Budget 14,000 dollars, raised 9,500 through a crowdfund and gig money.

projects.name: Spare-room hosting
projects.text: I rent the spare room when I'm on tour, about eight nights a month at 140 a night. A neighbour and sometime friend, Leila, does the changeovers for 50 a clean. It pays roughly a third of my rent. Superhost status brings the bookings. Reviews matter more than anything else about the listing.

projects.name: Student recital
projects.text: Want to put on a recital for my students in November, in a church hall in Enmore, for parents and friends. The youngest is nine, the oldest is sixty-one. Still need a venue and a PA.

notes.text: Tinnitus has been loud this week. Went to an audiologist, who said it's stable but I should wear moulded earplugs on stage. They cost 280. I've been wearing foam ones for ten years and swearing I'd upgrade. Ordered the moulds.

Marrickville session: three takes of 'Slow Ghosts', the third was it. Tom the bassist said I played behind the beat on purpose. I did. Don't know how to explain it to someone who hasn't been in the room.
Ex-partner still has my amp. A Fender Deluxe I bought in 2016, still sitting in her hallway in Dulwich Hill. I keep meaning to ask for it. She keeps not offering. Both of us pretending.

Got back from Melbourne. Three-star review on the listing from the guest who stayed while I was touring. Cleanliness, three stars. 'Bathroom floor was gritty, bedding smelled like dust.' I was in Melbourne. I texted Leila. She said she'd cleaned on Thursday. Maybe the guest was fussy. Maybe she missed a spot. Either way, one more review under four stars and I lose Superhost, and the hosting income pays a big chunk of my rent. I haven't told anyone.

Spent the morning scrubbing the bathroom myself, grout with a toothbrush. Washed every sheet in the house. Did not tell Leila. Don't want her to feel blamed. I owe her too much for the last-minute turnarounds.
Teaching: a thirty-nine-year-old accountant told me she's wanted to learn guitar since she was twelve. Taught her the intro to 'Blackbird'. She teared up on the third bar. I love this job.

Checked the Airbnb dashboard at 2 am. Four bookings next month, ninety-five percent occupancy while I'm away. If I can keep the rating above 4.8 I'm fine. If I slip I'll need to find 450 dollars a month from somewhere. Looked at my bank balance. Not great.
Wedding gig in Camden, Sunday, five hours of 'Fly Me to the Moon'. The bride's father requested 'Sweet Caroline' three times. Played it. He tipped fifty dollars. Don't tell the trio.
Leila texted she's going to Melbourne herself in October for a week and can't do the changeovers. Panic. Posted in a local Facebook group, nothing yet.

Had a mini-meltdown at the audiologist's follow-up about whether I should quit loud gigs. She said it's fine to keep playing if I protect my ears. I cried a bit in the car park. Not at the news, just the relief.

messages.text:
Tom: Can you do Tuesday for the mix review?
Me: Yes, 6 pm.
Tom: Bring the Ibanez.
Me: Always.

Me: How did the clean go on Thursday?
Leila: I did the whole place. Is there a problem?
Me: Just checking. All good.
Leila: I'm in Melbourne in October by the way.

Me: Can I pick up the amp this week?
Jess: Which weekend?
Me: Whichever.
Jess: I'll check.

Mum: Are you eating properly on tour?
Me: Yes.
Mum: What did you eat today?
Me: A banana.
Mum: Callum.

Ruth: I practiced every day this week!
Me: Brilliant.
Ruth: Even Sunday.
Me: You're ahead of me.

calendar.event: Melbourne tour, two shows, leave Thursday

relations.about: Bassist in Monday Ghosts, ten-year friend, stricter than he looks
Neighbour who cleans between guests, doing me a favour at fifty a time

constraints: Can't be home on tour weekends to check the rooms
Won't take wedding gigs on Sundays after October
Needs reliable cleaning on short notice
Won't change the listing price during tour weeks
sensitive: Rent is tight; the hosting income pays a big chunk of it
Hasn't told Leila about the review
